# Same-model review

**Same-model review: passed. Independent audit: not yet performed.**

## Correctness

**PASS.** The central construction is direct. If \(w\) belongs to the free subalgebra generated by the variables other than \(x_i\), then \(D_w(x_i)=w\) and \(D_w(x_j)=0\) lowers the number of occurrences of \(x_i\) in every monomial by one. This proves local nilpotence without auxiliary classification results. Abelianization sends \(D_w\) to \(\overline w\,\partial_{x_i}\), so the kernel and every fiber are exactly the kernel and fibers of \(B_i\to\overline B_i\). The homogeneous dimension formula follows by subtracting the degree-\(d\) dimensions of the free associative and commutative polynomial algebras.

The global rank threshold uses one external input only in rank two: Corollary 28 of Baltazar--Lopes--Morales states, under their standing algebraically closed characteristic-zero hypothesis, that \(\ker(\pi_*)\cap\operatorname{LND}(k\langle x,y\rangle)=\{0\}\). Rank one is trivial, while the explicit derivation \(D(x_1)=[x_2,x_3]\), \(D(x_j)=0\) for \(j\ge2\), proves failure in every rank at least three.

The isotropy statement was checked on generators: \(\tau_q(x_i)=x_i+q\) and \(\tau_q(x_j)=x_j\) commutes with \(D_w\) for every \(q,w\in B_i\). In characteristic zero, the exponential identity follows because \(D_w^2(x_i)=0\) and \(D_w\) kills all other generators.

## Originality

**PASS, to the best of our knowledge.** The closest recent source is arXiv:2609.19470v1. It proves the rank-two zero-detection statement and gives rank-two counterexamples showing that a locally nilpotent abelianization need not lift to a locally nilpotent derivation, but it does not state a higher-rank fiber theorem. Earlier papers by Crode--Shestakov and Drensky--Makar-Limanov concern locally nilpotent derivations of the rank-two free algebra. The Drensky--Yu survey concerns rank-three automorphisms and coordinates.

Searches using the exact and synonymous formulations “abelianization/commutativization of locally nilpotent derivations of a free associative algebra,” “rank-three locally nilpotent derivations,” “commutator ideal locally nilpotent derivation,” and the prototype \(D(x_1)=[x_2,x_3]\) did not locate the sharp threshold or the affine-fiber/Hilbert-series statement.

The full texts of the 2020 Crode--Shestakov paper and the 2007 Drensky--Yu survey were not inspected; available abstracts and bibliographic descriptions were checked. They are the most plausible older sources for an equivalent elementary observation under different terminology. The source arXiv preprint is also very recent and may be revised. Accordingly, no claim of exhaustive literature coverage is made.

## Value

**PASS.** The result turns a rank-two phenomenon in a new paper into a sharp rank threshold and identifies the mechanism of failure. Beginning with three generators, the abelianization map loses not merely isolated locally nilpotent derivations but an explicitly quantified infinite-dimensional family in every elementary triangular fiber. The exact kernel Hilbert series and the parallel invisible one-parameter automorphisms make the loss of information concrete and reusable.

## Scope of the claim

No novelty is claimed for the definition of elementary triangular derivations, for the fact that the abelianization kernel is the commutator ideal, for rank-two triangulability, or for the general theory of free-associative automorphisms. The claimed contribution is the higher-rank abelianization fiber theorem, its sharp rank-three onset, and the graded size formula for the locally nilpotent kernel described in `RESULT.md`.
